words.sense: Accusations exchanged in retaliation for other accusations.
misconceptions: Confused with incrimination when the defining clue is overlooked.

words.sense: Evidence or an allegation implicating someone in wrongdoing.
misconceptions: Confused with recrimination when the defining clue is overlooked.

semantic_axes.description: Recrimination is blame answered by blame; incrimination connects someone to wrongdoing through a charge or evidence.

edges.boundary_rule: Recrimination is blame answered by blame; incrimination connects someone to wrongdoing through a charge or evidence.
clues_a: Accusations exchanged in retaliation for other accusations.
clues_b: Material pointing to guilt or misconduct.
Evidence or an allegation implicating someone in wrongdoing.
irrelevant_clues: format, colour, or popularity unless they establish the boundary
location or timing that does not change the decisive feature

misconceptions.M1: Treating recrimination as though it always means incrimination.
misconceptions.M2: Treating incrimination as though it always means recrimination.
misconceptions.M3: Overvaluing a distracting detail instead of the decisive semantic distinction.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Amina’s reply to her roommate?

beats.text: After her roommate accused her of making the kitchen dirty, Amina accused the roommate of stealing her groceries.
beats.decisive_clue: she answered an accusation with another accusation
beats.reason: This establishes that she answered an accusation with another accusation.

beats.text: Her reply went on to list five other things her roommate had done wrong.
beats.decisive_clue: she answered an accusation with another accusation
beats.reason: The growing exchange confirms reciprocal blame rather than evidence connecting someone to a particular offence.

chains.feedback_short: She answered an accusation with another accusation; that detail favors recrimination.
chains.feedback_deep: The growing exchange confirms reciprocal blame rather than evidence connecting someone to a particular offence. Recrimination is blame answered by blame; incrimination connects someone to wrongdoing through a charge or evidence.
chains.contrast_rule: Recrimination answers blame; incrimination points to wrongdoing.
